q.intro.text: Which numbers x make the absolute value of x minus four equal to three? Pick an answer, and say how sure you are.

q.cb.right.text: You said x is one or seven, and you were right. Both are three away from four.

q.cb.one.text: You said only seven. It works, but so does one. One minus four is negative three, and its absolute value is three. The inside can be negative three too.

q.cb.pm.text: You said three or negative three. Those are values of the inside, x minus four. Then x minus four is three or negative three, so x is seven or one.

q.cb.none.text: x is one or seven: the two numbers three away from four.

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one. The graph moves first, then the notation.

e.step0.text: Inside first. The bars change their rule where the inside is zero. x minus four is zero at x equals four. That is the vertex of the graph, the point four, zero.

e.step1.text: Right of four the inside is positive, so the bars change nothing: x minus four. Left of four it is negative, so the bars take its opposite: four minus x. Two straight pieces make a V.

e.step2.text: Where is the V at height three? The line y equals three meets it twice, once on each piece. So there are two solutions.

e.step3.text: Solve each piece. x minus four equals three gives seven. Four minus x equals three gives one. So x is one or seven, both three away from four.

e.why.text: Quick check: why does four minus x equals three count too?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. Left of four the bars are four minus x, so that piece must equal three as well. It is the same as x minus four equals negative three.

e.why.parts.text: The bars act on the whole inside, not on each part. The absolute value of x minus four is not x plus four.

e.why.always.text: Not always two. An absolute value equal to zero has one solution, and equal to a negative number, none. Here the V meets the line twice.

t.intro.text: Your turn. Solve two times the absolute value of x minus two, minus four, equals six. The graph shows the left side.

t.iso.text: First step: what do you get when the absolute value is alone?

t.iso.ok.text: Right. Add four, then divide by two. The absolute value of x minus two is five.

t.iso.split.text: Not yet. Get the bars alone first. Only then split into two cases.

t.iso.sub.text: Undo the minus four by adding four. Then divide by two.

t.sol.text: Now split it into two cases and solve both.

t.sol.ok.text: Right. x minus two equals five gives seven, and x minus two equals negative five gives negative three. The line y equals six meets the V right there.

t.sol.pm.text: Five and negative five are values of x minus two. Add two in each case.

t.sol.other.text: x minus two equals five, or x minus two equals negative five. Solve each one.

p.intro.text: Jordan solves the absolute value of two x minus three equals negative five by splitting. Two x minus three equals negative five gives negative one, and two x minus three equals five gives four. He says the solutions are negative one and four. Is Jordan right?

p.test.text: Test his answers on the graph. Build the argument: tap a reason for each claim.

p.build.text: Build the argument: tap a reason for each claim.

p.c1.text: Yes. At negative one the inside is negative five, so that case does not hold there. The absolute value is five, not negative five.

p.c2.text: Yes. At four the inside is five, so the case where it is negative does not hold. The absolute value is five again.

p.c3.text: Yes. The V never dips below the x axis, so it never meets the line y equals negative five.

p.no.algebra.text: Correct algebra inside a case only counts where that case holds. Test the condition.

p.no.positive.text: You may not drop the minus. Equal to five is a different equation, with different solutions.

p.no.both.text: No number meets both conditions at once. A candidate only has to meet the condition of its own case.

p.no.other.text: True, but it does not back up this claim. Try it on another one.

p.done.text: Jordan is wrong. There is no solution. An absolute value is a distance, and a distance is never negative.
